chunks: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from al-Fuḍayl, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said, “Whoever dies not knowing his Imam, dies a death of Jāhiliyyah”? He said: “Yes.” I said: “A blind Jāhiliyyah of ignorance, or a Jāhiliyyah of not knowing his Imam?” He said: “A Jāhiliyyah of kufr, nifaq, and misguidance.”

key_terms.إِمَامَهُ: his Imam; the divinely designated leader whose recognition is religiously necessary
key_terms.جَهْلَاءَ: blind ignorance; simple or unrefined ignorance
key_terms.ضَلَالٍ: misguidance; straying from the true path
key_terms.كُفْرٍ: disbelief; rejection of truth in this context
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: a death of Jāhiliyyah; dying in a state likened to the pre-Islamic condition of deviation
key_terms.نِفَاقٍ: hypocrisy; inward opposition concealed by outward profession

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith ‘whoever dies without knowing his Imam dies a death of Jāhiliyyah’ mean?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the necessity of recognizing the Imam and portrays dying without that recognition as a death resembling Jāhiliyyah. The Imam عليه السلام explains that this is not mere lack of information, but a state tied to kufr, nifaq, and misguidance, highlighting the creedal significance of Imamate in Shia thought.
